content:
How to succeed with a Moka pot? Instant espresso a good alternative?
Hi, all! I live full time in an RV and I am currently 2 hours away from the closest large town, due to work. Normally I would go to a local coffee shop to get my tasty treats but the only coffee shop by me (a small, expensive cafe in a mountain resort town) has just ruined my trust and with them being so pricey, I would like to make my lattes and milk drinks at home again. 

I’ve battled internally since moving into an RV 3 years ago about wanting to buy an espresso machine, but given the size, lack of space and power consumption I just can’t find a way to justify it. I have a small Bialetti Moka pot (I think it is a 3-cup/\\\~4oz) but I have found I can’t get strong enough lattes from it. It makes great tasting black coffee, but the whole cow’s milkI use just really seems to wash it out. 

I almost always use espresso beans, grind my beans at home and keep them sealed in an airtight container, always to a salt-grain consistency and I turn the heat off once it starts percolating so as to not burn it. I use aeropress filters in the basket. I fill the basket up so it is a mound instead of flat. Is there anything else I can be doing to increase the potency, besides just getting a bigger Moka pot? 

Alternatively, I keep seeing Nescafé instant espresso online. Is this a good option? I don’t have very high hopes for espresso powder, but figure I can buy an entire jar of it for less than the price of one of the lattes near me so it couldn’t hurt to try. If it is not good though, I would prefer to not waste product or money. 

Any other creative solutions are also welcome! Thank you 😊
